title: Systems of equations
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

hints.alg.systems.graph: The solution is the point on both lines: where they cross. Same slope? Then they're parallel (no solution) or the same line (infinitely many).
hints.alg.systems.substitute: Put what y equals into the other equation, solve for x, then find y.
hints.alg.systems.eliminate: Add or subtract the equations so one letter cancels. If nothing cancels yet, multiply one equation first (every term).
hints.alg.systems: Find the point that works in both equations: substitute, eliminate, or read where the lines cross.

misconceptionMessages.alg.systems-swapped: Write the solution as (x, y): x first, then y.
misconceptionMessages.alg.systems-intercept: That's where one line crosses the y-axis. The solution is where the two lines cross each other.
misconceptionMessages.alg.systems-parallel-one: The slopes are the same, so the lines are parallel and never cross: no solution.
misconceptionMessages.alg.systems-same-line-one: Rewrite the second equation as y = mx + b. It's the same line, so every point on it works: infinitely many.
misconceptionMessages.alg.systems-same-line-none: Rewrite the second equation as y = mx + b. Same slope AND same intercept means the same line: infinitely many.
misconceptionMessages.alg.systems-distribute: When you put (x + 4) in for y, multiply everything inside: 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12.
misconceptionMessages.alg.systems-forgot-divide: Adding gave 2x, not x. Divide by 2 to get x.
misconceptionMessages.alg.systems-subtract-one-side: Whatever you do to the left side, do to the right side too: subtract the numbers on the right as well.
misconceptionMessages.alg.systems-multiply-one-side: Multiply every term of the equation, including the number on the right.

sections.title: Solve by graphing
sections.objective: Read the solution where two lines cross, and tell how many solutions a system has.
explain: A system is two equations that must both be true. Each equation is a line; the point on both lines makes both equations true.

steps: Solid line: y = 2x + 1.  Dashed line: y = −x + 4.

sections.key: The solution is where the lines cross, written (x, y). Parallel lines (same slope): no solution. The same line: infinitely many.

sections.title: Solve by substitution
sections.objective: Put what y equals into the other equation.
explain: When one equation already says what y is, you can swap that in for y in the other equation. Then there's only x left to solve.
sections.key: Swap in what y equals, solve for x, then put x back in to find y. Write (x, y) and check both equations.

sections.title: Solve by elimination
sections.objective: Add or subtract the equations so one letter cancels.
explain: Adding two true equations gives another true equation. If the y-terms are opposites, adding makes them disappear.
sections.key: Add (or subtract) so one letter cancels. If nothing cancels yet, multiply one whole equation first, both sides.

sections.title: Putting it together
explain: Now the systems are mixed. Use whichever method fits; only the solution counts.
sections.key: Find the point that works in both equations. Check it in both.
